title: Fast and Consistent Structure Learning in Graphical Models via Approximate Cross-Validation
abstract: arXiv:2611.30822v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Structure learning for sparse graphical models in high dimensions requires both computational scalability and selection consistency. Classical criteria such as (Extended) Bayesian Information Criterion can provide consistency, but rely on model-specific likelihoods and complexity calibration. In comparison, cross-validation avoids such analytic calibration and is therefore attractive for graph learning. However, cross-validation is computationally infeasible and theoretically inconsistent in structure learning. This creates a tension between consistency and flexibility in modeling. In this work, we resolve the tension by developing a scalable graph-recovery procedure built on approximate cross-validation. We demonstrate its effectiveness in learning large graphical models both theoretically and empirically, and establish selection consistency under mild signal strength assumptions.

translated_title: 通过近似交叉验证实现图模型中快速且一致的结构学习
translated_abstract: 高维稀疏图模型的结构学习既需要计算上的可扩展性，也需要选择一致性。经典准则如（扩展）贝叶斯信息准则可以提供一致性，但依赖于模型特定的似然函数和复杂度校准。相比之下，交叉验证避免了这种解析校准，因此在图学习中颇具吸引力。然而，交叉验证在结构学习中计算上不可行，且理论上不一致。这在建模的一致性与灵活性之间造成了张力。在本工作中，我们通过开发一种基于近似交叉验证的可扩展图恢复方法来化解这一矛盾。我们从理论和实证两方面展示了该方法在学习大型图模型方面的有效性，并在温和的信号强度假设下建立了选择一致性。
tldr: 本文提出基于近似交叉验证的可扩展图结构学习方法，解决了交叉验证在结构学习中计算不可行且理论不一致的问题，并在温和的信号强度假设下实现了选择一致性。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a scalable graph structure learning procedure based on approximate cross-validation, resolving the computational infeasibility and theoretical inconsistency of cross-validation in structure learning while establishing selection consistency under mild signal strength assumptions.
